extraction.name: C-E VAL
extraction.description: C-E VAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It consists of 13,948 multiple-choice questions spanning 52 diverse disciplines across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Yuzhuo Bai (Tsinghua University); Zhihao Zhu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Junlei Zhang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Jinghan Zhang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Tangjun Su (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Junteng Liu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Chuancheng Lv (Tsinghua University); Yikai Zhang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Jiayi Lei (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Yao Fu (University of Edinburgh); Maosong Sun (Tsinghua University); Junxian He (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
extraction.citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He. C-E VAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by sourcing mock exams and small-scale local exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. The data was primarily sourced as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and then parsed automatically or manually into a structured format.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Document analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The English subject for middle and high school levels and the middle school Chinese subject were excluded. Questions with fewer than four options were also eliminated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams and past exam questions from top Chinese universities and the Weipu website, primarily in the form of PDF or Microsoft Word documents, and a minor fraction as web pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the development split, which were then manually revised by the authors. The authors also manually parsed and validated the exam questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, and the machine-generated explanations were manually revised to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL will help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, and foster their development and growth for Chinese users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context; solve multiple-choice questions through prompting.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To facilitate the potential usage of C-E VAL in a few-shot COT setting, we combine automatic generation and human annotation to produce high-quality explanation data for the development split. Specifically, we first prompt GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanation to explain the ground-truth answer, then we manually revise the generated explanations to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format... For subjects with complex mathematical notations such as many subjects in the STEM category, we manually convert them into standard LATEX formats... we eliminate questions with fewer than four options and randomly drop incorrect choices for questions with more than four options. All questions also go through the standard data preprocessing pipeline, such as deduplication and cleaning.
